svg.title: A wider Gaussian potential suppresses large wavevector transfer
svg.desc: A one-dimensional Gaussian perturbation has fixed integrated strength g. Widths are ell0 and twice ell0. Real-space U ell0/g=(ell0/ell)/sqrt(2pi) exp[-x squared/(2ell squared)]. The Fourier intensity |U tilde/g| squared=exp[-q squared ell squared]. The transfer is q=k prime-k; physical momentum transfer is hbar q. The box-normalized one-dimensional plane-wave matrix element is M=U tilde(q)/mathcal L. These one-dimensional quantities are not a three-dimensional differential cross section.
